title: screening handoff sketch - candidate priyanka kumar
body:
Quick context: screen with Priyanka (resume: distributed systems + 3 yrs infra at a mid-size ML infra shop). This is my personal sketch to hand off to the loop owner. Rough, fuzzy — lots of "notes-to-self" and candidate quotes.

Signal buckets (what stood out):
- Systems thinking: good at tracing end-to-end request path (frontend -> router -> runtime -> kv cache) and articulated tradeoffs for caching vs latency. Gave a concrete example of prefix caching invalidation they implemented (TTL-based + version stamping).
- Inference/LLM intuition: general awareness of KV cache and batching, but limited low-level detail on attention optimizations or quantization. Said they'd "learn" but hasn't shipped quantized models.
- Debug/ops: anecdotal incident where they debugged OOM on a multi-tenant g4 pool using memprofs; solution was conservative (reduced max_batch_size) — practical but not creative.
- Collaboration/communication: clear explainer, good at drawing diagrams on whiteboard.

Red flags / gaps to watch for:
- No hands-on experience with compiled kernels or autotuning stacks (no JIT compiler exposure).
- Limited exposure to SLO-driven routing or multi-model fallbacks — theoretical understanding only.
- Ops tooling: hasn't used HSM/KMS integration flows; security experience primarily config-level.

Memorable quotes: "I prefer conservative rollouts — I like having a fallback baked in before traffic hits new kernels." Good mindset for reliability but check for ability to balance cost/latency tradeoffs.

Coding exercise notes (short internal test I gave):
- Problem: simple streaming tokenizer + small sliding-window KV cache simulation. Priyanka's approach: correct architecture, edge cases handled, missed an off-by-one in evict logic (caught in pair-debug). Implementation was readable but not optimal for throughput. Estimated improvement: ~15% by changing data structures and avoiding copies.

Suggested onsite focuses (if we move forward):
- Deep dive: prompt them to sketch a low-latency batching design and probe specific kernel-level optimizations (attention cache layout, kv cache eviction heuristics).
- Ops scenario: present a degraded-region incident with fallback routing needs; ask for step-by-step mitigation and eventual permanent fix.
- Take-home option: small perf tuning task on a toy transformer in repo (quantize + measure latency/cost), but only if we want to test learning curve for quantization.

Recommendation / next step: lean-pass to loop. Candidate shows strong systems instincts and good communication; gaps in ML-specialized infra (quantization, kernel tooling) can be mitigated if we pair them with an applied-ml mentor for first 6-8 weeks. I’d recommend a 2-hour onsite focusing on system design + ops incident response.

Action items (for loop owner):
- Assign Maya to lead design deep-dive (first 30m).
- Prepare short perf artifact if we want a take-home (GH branch + brief).
- Note compensation constraints (candidate asked about flexibility around base vs equity; flagged for Recruiter).

Notes-to-self: ask Priyanka about specific profiling tools (did they use nvprof/nsys or only generic profilers?) and whether they have any private repos with perf experiments we can look at. Also confirm timezone for scheduling: IST preferred afternoons.
